topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under the Nebraska Real Estate License Act, who serves as chairperson of the State Real Estate Commission?
choice_a: The Secretary of State
choice_b: The Governor
choice_c: The Attorney General
choice_d: A broker member elected annually by the commission
explanation: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.07(1)(a) creates the State Real Estate Commission and provides that it 'shall consist of the Secretary of State, who shall be chairperson of the commission, and six members appointed by the Governor.' The Secretary of State's chairmanship is a statutory ex officio role, not an elected or rotating position among the appointed commissioners.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: How many members does the Governor appoint to the State Real Estate Commission (in addition to the Secretary of State), and how many of them must be active, licensed brokers appointed one from each of Nebraska's three congressional districts?
choice_a: Eight members total; four district brokers
choice_b: Six members total; three district brokers
choice_c: Five members total; two district brokers
choice_d: Seven members total; three district brokers
explanation: Section 81-885.07(1)(a)-(b) provides for six members appointed by the Governor. Three of those six must be active and licensed real estate brokers (or associate brokers) with at least five years' experience, appointed one from each of the state's three congressional districts, with the total commission (including the Secretary of State) numbering seven.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Beyond the three district broker members, §81-885.07(1)(c) requires the remaining three at-large gubernatorial appointees to the Commission to include which combination?
choice_a: Two public members and one broker
choice_b: Three brokers, with no minimum experience requirement
choice_c: One member representative of the public, one licensed salesperson with at least three years' real estate experience, and one licensed broker with at least five years' experience
choice_d: One attorney, one licensed appraiser, and one public member
explanation: Section 81-885.07(1)(c) requires the three remaining appointed seats to be filled at large: one representative of the public, one licensed salesperson who has engaged in the business for at least three years, and one active, licensed broker with at least five years' experience — mirroring the experience threshold used for the district broker seats.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What is the maximum length of service an appointed Commission member may serve in a single appointment cycle under §81-885.07(2)?
choice_a: Two six-year terms
choice_b: Four-year terms with unlimited reappointment
choice_c: A lifetime appointment subject to Senate confirmation
choice_d: One six-year term, in addition to any partial term previously served to fill a vacancy
explanation: Section 81-885.07(2) states that upon expiration of a member's term, the Governor appoints a successor for a term of six years, and 'any appointed member shall be limited to one six-year term, in addition to any partial term served.' This prevents an appointee who filled an unexpired vacancy from also serving a full six-year term afterward without limit.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: How many members of the State Real Estate Commission must be present at an official meeting to constitute a quorum?
choice_a: Four
choice_b: Three
choice_c: Five
choice_d: Six, requiring unanimous appointed-member attendance
explanation: Section 81-885.07(2) fixes the quorum requirement at 'not less than four members of the commission,' and provides that the action of a majority of members present is deemed the action of the commission.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Section 81-885.07(2) restricts appointed commissioners from doing what while serving on the Commission?
choice_a: Practicing real estate brokerage privately
choice_b: Holding any other elective or appointive state or federal office
choice_c: Residing outside the congressional district they represent after appointment
choice_d: Serving more than four consecutive years without reappointment
explanation: Section 81-885.07(2) provides that 'no appointed person may act as a member of the commission while holding any other elective or appointive state or federal office.' This is a dual-office-holding restriction, not a restriction on continuing to practice real estate.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §81-885.07(4), what restriction applies specifically to the Commission's director and any of its employees?
choice_a: They must hold an active real estate broker's license
choice_b: They must be reappointed by the Governor every two years
choice_c: Neither the director nor any commission employee may be an officer or paid employee of any real estate association or group of real estate dealers or brokers
choice_d: They must personally co-sign every licensee's trust account statement
explanation: Section 81-885.07(4) provides that the commission employs a director to keep records and act as custodian of commission files, and expressly states that 'neither the director nor any employee of the commission may be an officer or paid employee of any real estate association or group of real estate dealers or brokers,' guarding against conflicts of interest with the industry the agency regulates.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What general rulemaking authority does §81-885.07(5) grant the Commission?
choice_a: Authority to amend the Nebraska Real Estate License Act itself without legislative action
choice_b: Authority to set criminal penalties for unlicensed real estate practice
choice_c: Authority to override formal legal opinions issued by the Attorney General
choice_d: Authority to adopt and promulgate rules and regulations relating to the administration of, and not inconsistent with, the Nebraska Real Estate License Act
explanation: Section 81-885.07(5) grants the commission the power to 'adopt and promulgate rules and regulations relating to the administration of but not inconsistent with the act.' This administrative rulemaking power is bounded — the Commission cannot create rules that conflict with the statute itself, and cannot amend the underlying Act, which remains the Legislature's role.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §81-885.07(6), what educational activity is the Commission expressly authorized to conduct or assist in conducting, at the Commission's expense?
choice_a: Real estate institutes and seminars, open to all licensees
choice_b: Mandatory continuing legal education programs for attorneys
choice_c: Public school curricula on housing policy
choice_d: Certification programs for property tax appraisers
explanation: Section 81-885.07(6) authorizes the commission to 'conduct or assist in conducting real estate institutes and seminars and incur and pay the necessary expenses in connection therewith,' provided such institutes or seminars are open to all licensees, not a select group.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §81-885.07(7), what standard governs how the Commission sets the fees it charges for its services?
choice_a: Fees may be set at whatever rate maximizes the agency's cash reserves
choice_b: Fees must be reasonable, not exceed the actual cost of the service, and be set at a level necessary to meet Legislature-approved expenditures while maintaining a sufficient cash fund balance
choice_c: A single flat statewide fee schedule set by the Legislature each biennium
choice_d: The Commission is prohibited from charging fees; it is funded entirely from general tax revenue
explanation: Section 81-885.07(7) authorizes the commission to 'charge reasonable fees for services it renders, not to exceed the actual costs thereof,' with fees set 'at the level necessary to meet expenditures of the commission as approved by the Legislature and to provide a sufficient cash fund balance.' The Commission is a cash-funded agency operating largely on license and service fees rather than general tax appropriations.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §81-885.10(1), which of the following is NOT among the disciplinary tools the Commission may use against a licensee found guilty of a violation?
choice_a: Revoking or suspending the license
choice_b: Entering into a consent decree
choice_c: Ordering imprisonment of the licensee
choice_d: Issuing a cease and desist order to a violator of §81-885.03
explanation: Section 81-885.10(1) empowers the commission to revoke or suspend licenses, censure licensees, enter consent decrees, issue cease and desist orders, and impose civil fines. The Commission is an administrative licensing body with civil and administrative remedies — it has no authority to impose criminal penalties such as imprisonment; that authority rests with the courts.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: What is the statutory cap on the civil fine the Commission may impose for each complaint under §81-885.10(1)?
choice_a: A flat $500 regardless of the circumstances
choice_b: The lesser of $1,000 or the buyer's actual damages
choice_c: There is no statutory cap on the fine amount
choice_d: The greater of $5,000 or the total amount of commission earned by the licensee in each transaction subject to the complaint
explanation: Section 81-885.10(1) caps the total civil fine per complaint at 'the greater of five thousand dollars or the total amount of commission earned by the licensee in each transaction that is subject to the complaint,' allowing the fine to scale upward in high-value transactions rather than being limited to a flat dollar figure.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §81-885.10(2), does the Commission retain authority to discipline a person for past conduct after that person's real estate license lapses or is not renewed?
choice_a: Yes; the Commission retains its powers under the section with respect to the licensee's actions regardless of whether he or she continues to be licensed
choice_b: No, all disciplinary jurisdiction ends the moment licensure lapses
choice_c: Only if the person reapplies for licensure within 90 days
choice_d: Only if a court first enters an order reinstating the Commission's jurisdiction
explanation: Section 81-885.10(2) provides that 'the commission shall retain its powers under this section with respect to the actions of a licensee, whether or not he or she continues to be licensed under the act.' A licensee cannot avoid accountability for misconduct that occurred while licensed simply by letting the license lapse.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §81-885.21(7), what rulemaking discretion does the Commission have regarding the trust account maintenance requirements that otherwise apply to active brokers?
choice_a: It must require every licensed broker to maintain at least two separate trust accounts
choice_b: It may adopt and promulgate rules and regulations exempting active brokers who have no trust account activity and no anticipated trust account activity from the trust account requirements
choice_c: It may waive trust accounting requirements for any broker with more than ten years' experience
choice_d: It has no authority to grant exemptions; any exemption requires a legislative amendment
explanation: Section 81-885.21(7) gives the commission specific rulemaking authority to exempt from the trust account requirements those active brokers who have no trust account activity and none anticipated — a targeted regulatory carve-out, not a blanket experience-based waiver or an all-or-nothing legislative matter.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §81-885.24, when is the Commission required — rather than merely permitted — to investigate the actions of a broker, associate broker, salesperson, or subdivider?
choice_a: Only after the licensee has been criminally convicted
choice_b: Only during the biennial license renewal cycle
choice_c: Upon the sworn written complaint of any person; the Commission may additionally investigate on its own motion
choice_d: Only when the matter is referred to it by the Attorney General
explanation: Section 81-885.24 provides that the commission 'may, upon its own motion, and shall, upon the sworn complaint in writing of any person, investigate the actions' of a licensee. The 'shall' language makes investigation mandatory once a proper sworn written complaint is filed, while investigation on the Commission's own initiative remains discretionary.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Before the Commission may censure a licensee, impose a civil fine, revoke or suspend a license, or issue a cease and desist order, what does §81-885.25(1) require the Commission to do first?
choice_a: Publish the charges in a newspaper of general circulation
choice_b: Obtain a search warrant from a district court
choice_c: Refer the matter exclusively to the county attorney for prosecution
choice_d: Send the licensee or violator a copy of the written complaint by mail and, unless the right to a hearing is waived through a consent order, give the licensee a hearing on the charges
explanation: Section 81-885.25(1) requires the commission to send the licensee or violator a copy of the complaint (by registered mail, certified mail, tracked first-class mail, or a designated delivery service) containing the charges, and to provide a hearing unless the person waives that right and executes a consent order — this is the statutory due-process gateway before any of these sanctions may be imposed.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §81-885.25(2), if the person facing disciplinary charges is a licensed associate broker or salesperson, who else must the Commission notify of the hearing's date and place?
choice_a: The licensee's employing broker, by mailing a copy of the notice to the broker's last-known business address
choice_b: No one else needs to be notified
choice_c: The Commission's liability insurance carrier
choice_d: Every other licensee affiliated with the same brokerage
explanation: Section 81-885.25(2) requires at least twenty days' advance written notice of the hearing to the licensee or violator, and additionally provides that 'if the licensee is an associate broker or a salesperson, the commission shall also notify the broker employing the licensee by mailing a copy of such notice to the broker's last-known business address.'

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §81-885.26, how long does a licensee have to file a sworn answer after being served with a complaint and hearing notice, and what limitation does the statute place on that answer?
choice_a: 10 days, and the answer may include counterclaims for monetary damages
choice_b: 20 days, and the answer must contain all defenses the licensee intends to assert; no motions or other pleadings are authorized
choice_c: 30 days, and only a general denial is permitted
choice_d: There is no deadline; an answer may be filed any time before the hearing begins
explanation: Section 81-885.26 provides: 'Within twenty days from the time of service of the complaint and notice the licensee may file his or her sworn answer thereto which shall contain all defenses which he or she intends to assert. No motions or other pleadings shall be authorized.' This streamlines the pre-hearing process by requiring all defenses to be consolidated into a single sworn answer.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: In preparing for and conducting a Commission disciplinary hearing, who holds the statutory power under §81-885.27 to issue and sign subpoenas compelling witness attendance and document production?
choice_a: Only a district court judge
choice_b: Only the Attorney General
choice_c: The director, who has the power to issue and sign subpoenas requiring the attendance and testimony of witnesses and the production of papers, books, or documents
choice_d: Any licensed broker sitting as a volunteer hearing officer
explanation: Section 81-885.27 vests subpoena power in the director for purposes of hearing preparation, while the chairperson or any commission member may administer oaths, examine witnesses, and receive evidence at the hearing itself. The charged party also has the right to obtain a subpoena from the director for witnesses of their own choosing.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: How is an appeal from a final order of the State Real Estate Commission handled under §81-885.30?
choice_a: It is heard exclusively by the Commission itself on a motion for rehearing
choice_b: Final Commission orders are not subject to appeal
choice_c: The appeal must be filed directly with the Governor's office
choice_d: The appeal proceeds in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act
explanation: Section 81-885.30 states simply that 'an order of the commission which has become final may be appealed, and the appeal shall be in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act,' placing Commission appeals within Nebraska's standard framework for judicial review of agency action rather than a special real-estate-specific appellate process.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §81-885.21(3), how frequently must a broker's trust account be examined by a duly authorized representative of the Commission?
choice_a: Annually, or at such other time as the Commission may direct
choice_b: Never, unless a written complaint is first filed
choice_c: Only once, at the time of initial license renewal
choice_d: Monthly, without exception
explanation: Section 81-885.21(3) requires each broker to authorize the commission to examine the required trust account, and specifies that 'such examination shall be made annually or at such time as the commission may direct' — giving the Commission both a routine annual audit function and discretion to examine accounts at other times as circumstances warrant.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: If a broker refuses to submit trust account books and records for inspection, and the Commission concludes the trust account is in an unsafe or unsound condition, what does §81-885.22 direct the Commission to do?
choice_a: Immediately revoke the broker's license with no hearing
choice_b: Submit a complete report to the Attorney General, who may bring an action to enjoin the broker and, where warranted, seek appointment of a receiver over the broker's property and business
choice_c: Refer the matter directly to the Federal Bureau of Investigation
choice_d: Publicly post the broker's name on a statutory 'Wall of Shame' list
explanation: Section 81-885.22 requires the commission to 'forthwith submit a complete report to the Attorney General' when a broker fails to comply with trust account provisions or refuses inspection. The Attorney General may then bring an injunction action, and the reviewing court may appoint a receiver over the broker's property and business under §81-885.22-.23, with the Attorney General also empowered to appoint special counsel to prosecute the action.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §81-885.13(6), what is the consequence for an applicant who fails the required written broker or salesperson examination?
choice_a: The applicant is automatically granted a provisional license pending a retake
choice_b: The Commission must waive the examination requirement after a single failed attempt
choice_c: Failure to pass the examination is grounds for denial of a license without further hearing
choice_d: The applicant may appeal the failing score directly to district court before being permitted to retake the exam
explanation: Section 81-885.13(6) requires each broker and salesperson applicant to pass a written examination covering matters confronting that license type, and expressly states that 'failure to pass the examination shall be grounds for denial of a license without further hearing.' An applicant who passes must then complete all remaining license requirements within thirty days.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: Section 81-885.13(6) provides that the required license examination 'may be taken before the commission or any person designated by the commission.' What is the practical significance of this language for Nebraska's licensing exam today?
choice_a: It has no current practical effect; all exams are still administered in person before the Commission itself
choice_b: It means only a sitting Commission member may proctor an examination
choice_c: It requires that all examinations be administered exclusively at the Commission's Lincoln office
choice_d: It supplies the statutory basis for the Commission's current arrangement with Pearson VUE, which administers the computer-based licensing exam on the Commission's behalf
explanation: The statute's authorization for examination 'before the commission or any person designated by the commission' is the enabling language that lets the Commission delegate day-to-day exam administration to a third-party testing vendor rather than proctoring exams itself. In practice, the Nebraska Real Estate Commission has designated Pearson VUE to deliver the broker and salesperson licensing examinations at Pearson VUE testing centers.

topic: Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission
question: How does the Nebraska Real Estate Commission coordinate candidate eligibility with Pearson VUE, its designated third-party exam administrator?
choice_a: The Commission electronically transmits candidate authorization information to Pearson VUE on a daily basis, so that only candidates the Commission has approved may sit for the exam
choice_b: Pearson VUE independently verifies candidate eligibility using the Nebraska Secretary of State's business registration database
choice_c: Candidates self-certify their own eligibility directly to Pearson VUE, with no Commission involvement
choice_d: The Commission has no ongoing role once an applicant has been approved to test
explanation: Consistent with the delegation authority in §81-885.13(6), Pearson VUE's own published Nebraska real estate candidate information confirms that 'Pearson receives information daily from the Nebraska Real Estate Commission, authorizing candidates for the examination' — meaning the Commission, not the testing vendor, controls who is eligible to sit for the exam, with Pearson VUE handling only scheduling and delivery.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(6); Pearson VUE Nebraska Real Estate candidate information (pearsonvue.com)
